_: models.json — the models this stack was built and measured against, with their cards.
WHY A FILE AND NOT PROSE. The setup panel and docs/SETUP.md were going to carry two
copies of one list, and the copy nobody re-checked would be the one somebody followed
(AGENTS.md §0). This is the list; the panel reads it through /v1/setup and the doc
points here. Nothing in the running stack loads a model FROM here — the profile does
that. This is a recommendation, and it says so.
It is also the one file the export scrub is told to leave alone: every rule that
generalises the operator's own model would rewrite the very ids that make this useful.
`role` is what the model does in this stack; `note` is the honest reason to pick it.

engine.note: A 26B mixture-of-experts with ~4B active: the quality of a mid-size dense model at the speed and VRAM of a small one, which is what makes a companion that thinks in real time possible on one consumer GPU. Anything OpenAI-compatible works; this is what the decode knobs in profiles/companion.toml were tuned on.

recommended.note: the instruction-tuned weights. For vLLM, TGI, or transformers.
Google's own quantisation-aware-trained q4_0. The best quality-per-byte of the 4-bit builds; load this in LM Studio or llama-server if you have ~16 GB to give it.
the full quant ladder, Q2 through F16 — start here if the QAT build does not fit.
the base (not instruction-tuned). For fine-tuning, not for talking to.

sidecars.role: the librarians — small CPU models that embed, retrieve, judge and read for her
sidecars.note: Never her voice. They run on the CPU beside the engine so that recall, page-reading and yes/no judging cost no GPU time. All of [aux] ships OFF; docs/AUX-MODELS.md is the ledger of what each one does and what stays dark.

recommended.note: the chat sidecar: deep recall, reading a fetched page down to what was asked, yes/no judging. Q8_0 is ~1.3 GB and answers in well under a second on CPU.
the same model unquantised, if you serve it through vLLM instead.
the embedding sidecar — the semantic half of recall. Without it (or the sp-daemon's own L5) embeddings fall back to a hash space, which is honest but blunt.
late-interaction rerank. OFF by default and measured before it is armed — see docs/SEMANTICS.md for the experiment that a plain cosine rank won.

voice_in.role: the ear — speech to text, if you want to talk to her out loud
voice_in.note: Optional. [engine].asr_url points at any /v1/audio/transcriptions endpoint; the sp-daemon backend can also take audio frames natively.

recommended.note: streaming ASR, 4B. The realtime variant is the one worth having — batch ASR makes a conversation feel like a form submission.
the same, quantised, for a CPU or a small card.

hosted.role: the optional paid surface — her voice out, her pictures, live search
hosted.note: ONE key, four features, all of them off until the key file exists. Nothing in the memory system, the personality, the room or the gates needs it: an offline Kairos is a complete Kairos, minus a face she can grow and a voice that is not a local synth.
